start.name: Edfu (Idfu) city, Aswan Governorate, Egypt — GASCO transmission-line delivery point serving two sugar/paper factories and city households
start.coord_basis: Town centroid of Edfu/Idfu, Aswan Governorate — an independently geocodable Nile-valley town (reused from prior sweep); corroborated by three independent sources (Argaam, Youm7 2022, Al-Masry Al-Youm) describing the 37km/12in GASCO line delivering gas to Edfu's sugar/paper factories and households

end.name: UNRESOLVED — no source names the specific valve-room/tie-in point where the 37km Edfu spur leaves the GASCO Dahshour–Aswan ('Upper Egypt'/'South Valley') transmission trunk. The only concrete named candidate found — a real, SCADA-controlled gas pressure-reduction & metering station at Kom Ombo (confirmed by Ahram Gate + ElBalad; ElBalad states it supplies Edfu, Nasr al-Nuba, and Kom Ombo) — is DEFINITIVELY RULED OUT: Kom Ombo town (24.467N, 32.950E per Wikipedia) is ~57km straight-line from Edfu (24.9781N, 32.8749E), which is geometrically impossible for a 37km pipeline to span. The true tie-in must be much closer to Edfu than Kom Ombo, but no source names it.
end.coord_basis: No independently geocodable tie-in point identified — standing rule against fabricating or substituting an unconfirmed location

notes: Retry pass upgrades the prior researcher's evidence but does not resolve the tie-in. Two NEW sources this pass: ElBalad (elbalad.news/6735224) profiles a real, named, SCADA-controlled gas pressure-reduction & metering station at Kom Ombo (120M EGP, 2,500 sqm, 20,000 m3/h capacity) and explicitly states it serves >200,000 residents across Edfu, Nasr al-Nuba, and Kom Ombo (25,000 customers, 'Decent Life' initiative); Ahram Gate (gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5306934.aspx) independently confirms the Aswan governor touring this same 'محطة تخفيض ضغط وقياس الغاز الطبيعى' at Kom Ombo. This is a stronger, more specific candidate than the prior pass had (which only had loose 'Kom Ombo is nearby' reasoning) — BUT plugging in verified real-world coordinates (Kom Ombo town 24.467N/32.950E vs Edfu 24.9781N/32.8749E) shows they are ~57km apart in a straight line, which a 37km pipeline cannot span. This definitively rules out Kom Ombo TOWN as the tie-in (previously only flagged as a 'loose bound' at an incorrectly-estimated 15-20km). The station described in ElBalad may be a genuinely real GASCO/Egypt Gas asset that supplies Edfu via LOCAL distribution mains (a separate lower-pressure layer, not necessarily sited in Kom Ombo town itself, and not necessarily the point where the 37km TRANSMISSION spur taps the trunk) — so the actual physical location of whatever station serves this role could be well north of Kom Ombo town, closer to Edfu, but no source pins that location. Recommend leaving at ROUTE_PARTIAL (corridor-only) pending a GASCO network map or tender document naming the tie-in station explicitly; RouteAccuracy capped at 'low'.

notes: The pipeline itself is now IDENTIFIED and independently verified (I downloaded and text-extracted the PDF myself and confirmed the exact line): EGAS Annual Report 2018 (egyptoil-gas.com), page 20 of the PDF, table 'NATIONAL GAS GRID PIPELINES UNDER CONSTRUCTION DURING 2017/2018' — 'Project Rehabilitation gas supply pipeline 24" Fayoum / Giza 27 km', target end date December 2018 — listed alongside other real, GEM-tracked onshore trunk segments (Dahshur/AlWaste 68.5km, Ezdwaj Edku/Abu Houmas 30km, AlWaste/Beni Suef 60km, Tina/Abu Sultan 92km). The 24-inch diameter and 27km length match the sheet's recorded attributes exactly, strongly indicating this IS the sheet's own underlying (uncited-in-our-payload) source. This rules out the prior pass's exhaustive negative search (Ministry Decrees 1883/1884, Solaimaneyah-North Giza) — this is a THIRD, separate EGAS rehabilitation project not covered by those decrees. HOWEVER the report names only the governorates 'Fayoum' and 'Giza' with no station, town, or landmark for either end, so no defensible endpoint coordinates can be derived without guessing at a specific place — hence still unresolved for geometry. One unconfirmed lead worth flagging: the same report separately lists 'Giza West' as one of 9 sites where land was purchased for pressure-reduction stations (PRSs) under a DIFFERENT, unrelated IBRD/AFD-funded household gas-connection project (p.23 of the PDF) — a real, named place in Giza Governorate, but not confirmed to be the same project/pipeline as this 24in/27km rehabilitation line. Do not confuse this pipeline with an unrelated ~69km offshore 'Fayoum'/'Giza' gas-field-to-Rosetta-plant project (West Nile Delta) — different length/diameter, does not match this PID's recorded attributes. Recommend a follow-up search specifically for 'Giza West' PRS location or an EGAS/GASCO tender/as-built document naming the exact 27km rehabilitation route before attempting geometry.

notes: RESOLVED by main-session adjudication (2026-07-30) after the research agent marked it unresolved: the World Bank Implementation Completion Report 'Fourth and Kureimat Power Projects' (Loans 3103/3441-EGT) — the same document that resolved P8021 — names this exact pipeline twice: 'the diameter of the 160-km pipeline from Zafarana to Kureimat was changed from 20 inches to 18 inches' (detailed-design change, para on cost estimates) and 'EGPC has already completed the installation of the Zafarana-Kureimat pipeline in November 1995' alongside 'the foreign exchange funding for the 162km pipeline from Zafarana to Kureimat' (para 3.8). The 162 km as-built length matches the sheet's 163 km almost exactly. Verified by downloading the PDF and extracting text with pdftotext (the 3.9MB scanned PDF is a documented url_verifier large-PDF substring false-negative: HTTP 200, content check unreadable by the extractor). This withdraws the research agent's misattribution concern: the Sadat City→Dahshur 75km/42in GASCO line (Youm7 2013) is a SECOND, later Kureimat supply line, not a competing identity — Kureimat demonstrably has both. Sheet-facing intel for a future values pass (not this route batch): StartYear1 is blank on the sheet, WB gives completion November 1995; as-designed diameter 18in (changed from 20in). Kureimat endpoint coordinate consistent with P8021's anchor (ueepc.com); Zaafarana coordinate is the locality geocode — the exact compressor/tie-in site within Zaafarana is not separately published, so RouteAccuracy stays at the endpoints-method cap.
